description:
Found s468bc while rebasing #1037 onto main `9bee19b`.

`Pl/t/artifact-staleness-01.t` discovers the three checked-in transpiled
artifacts (cl/pcl-pack.lisp, cl/pcl-mro.lisp, cl/pcl-warnings.lisp) by their
line-1 `gen=` stamp and fails a row when that stamp is behind
`*pcl-cache-generation*`.  That catches "generation bumped, artifact not
regenerated".  It does NOT catch the other half: an artifact whose stamp is
CURRENT but whose BODY is not what the current compiler emits.

MEASURED on `9bee19b`: cl/pcl-pack.lisp was stamped gen=v2-611, the tree's own
generation, and the gate was green -- but regenerating it on a `9bee19b`
worktree produced a DIFFERENT body (pretty-printer line breaking around the
new `(p-let (($x :class ...)))` declaration entries, ~134 lines).  The proof
that it was main's drift and not a branch's change: the body regenerated on a
9bee19b worktree and the body regenerated on the #1037 branch are BYTE-EQUAL
(diff = 0 lines).  BD's own regeneration fixed the instance in `0e0b0b9`, so
this task is about the INSTRUMENT, not that artifact.

The check is cheap and exact: regenerate each artifact into a temp file and
compare the BODY (everything after line 1, and for pack everything before the
hand-written appendix).  Cost is one `pl2cl --extension` per artifact, which
is what `tools/rebuild-pack` already pays; if that is too slow for the gate,
the same comparison belongs in the WHAT-TO-RUN-WHEN row that bumps the
generation.

Guard: the row must FAIL on a tree where an artifact body has been perturbed
by one line.

=== DONE (s470c) ===

SHIPPED on 9083d2e (commit "s470c (Opus): #1072 — the artifact-staleness row
REGENERATES each artifact and compares the BODY, not only the gen= stamp").

Pl/t/artifact-staleness-01.t: three new rows (5 -> 8) on the SAME stamp-based
discovery loop.  Each discovered artifact is rebuilt into a temp file (never
in the tree) and everything after line 1 is compared; line 1 is the stamp,
which the existing rows own.  A mismatch names the artifact, the first
differing LINE NUMBER in it, the regeneration command, and prints a 40-line
head ('-' checked in, '+' regenerated, ' ' agreeing, stopping three agreeing
lines after the last difference).

The recipes are RUN, never re-spelled in the test:
  cl/pcl-pack.lisp      tools/rebuild-pack -o <tmp>       (new option)
  cl/pcl-mro.lisp       ./pl2cl --extension lib/mro.pm + tools/tag-license
  cl/pcl-warnings.lisp  ./pl2cl --extension lib/warnings.pm + tools/tag-license

tools/rebuild-pack gained -o PATH / --output PATH: write the result there and
leave the tree untouched (a relative path resolves against the CALLER's cwd,
resolved BEFORE the script cd's to the repo root; the "now run pack.t" hint is
printed only for an in-tree install; unknown argument / missing path exit 2).
The hand-written appendix still comes from the checked-in cl/pcl-pack.lisp,
which is its only home — so only the GENERATED part can move the row.

NORMALISATION: none, and that is a measurement.  --extension emits no program
preamble (#349), so no absolute path reaches an artifact (grep /home/ cl/*.lisp
finds nothing; Pl/t/extension-preamble-01.t is the guard; #217's build-machine
paths are gone).  The one caller-dependent thing is THE SOURCE PATH AS SPELLED:
`./pl2cl --extension /abs/.../lib/mro.pm` differs from `./pl2cl --extension
lib/mro.pm` in two lines, because a die in the module becomes the literal
"lib/mro.pm line 71" in the emitted CL.  Answer: run the recipe verbatim (cwd =
repo root, the recipe's relative spelling), not a normaliser.  Two runs are then
byte-equal (probed on mro and on pack).

RULE 12: an artifact the stamp loop discovers and %RECIPE cannot classify DIES
naming it.  Proved with a fourth stamped file (cl/pcl-zzz-fake.lisp): the three
real rows run and print first, then the file dies naming it.

GUARD (the task's bar), one artifact at a time, comment line perturbed:
  cl/pcl-mro.lisp      line 18 -> row 6 fails naming it, others green
  cl/pcl-warnings.lisp line 18 -> row 8 fails naming it, others green
  cl/pcl-pack.lisp     line 36 -> row 7 fails naming it, others green
restored -> 8/8 pass.

WALL TIME (the question the brief said to report, not decide): prove --timer on
a quiet box, this file 25 ms -> 3.56 s; the gate's slowest file in the same run
is Pl/t/autoviv-01.t at 130.6 s.  2.7 % of the slowest file, and the gate's wall
~= its slowest file, so the gate does not move.  (Loaded cold gate: 7.8 s vs
399.8 s — same ratio.)  The fallback this task names — running the comparison
from rebuild-pack-style tooling or a WHAT-TO-RUN-WHEN row instead of the gate —
is therefore NOT needed and was NOT implemented.

BARS: cold PCLXS_DIR=~/pclxs tools/prove-core = 199 files / 6796 rows, FAIL only
on the 13 known pclxs xs rows (xs-01 5/6, xs-02 4/4, xs-03 4/4).
tools/corpus-diff.pl 9083d2e = emission identical across 111 files, silent drops
5 unchanged.  No generation bump (a test and a tool changed; nothing under Pl/).
No sweep, no companion (excluded by the brief).

CI shape: the comparison needs nothing outside the checkout but perl (File::Temp
is core), PPI, Moo and sbcl — the Pl/t/core-deps-01.t set — plus the POSIX shell
utilities tools/rebuild-pack already used (sh, mktemp, sed, cat, cp).

NOT DONE: the three copies of the gen-stamp discovery loop (this file,
Pl/t/no-hardcoded-paths-01.t, Pl/t/extension-preamble-01.t) were left alone —
the USER's s413 dup-census scope makes test files not an extraction target.
subject: artifact-staleness-01.t compares the gen= STAMP only, so a checked-in artifact can be BODY-stale within its own generation
